text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight a war against emus. The emus won.
Western Australia. A drought sends about twenty thousand emus into the wheat fields, flattening crops and fences.
The farmers ask for help. The army sends Major Meredith, two machine guns, and ten thousand rounds.
First ambush: the emus walk right up to the dam. The gun fires a few shots, and jams.
So they bolt a gun onto a truck. But emus sprint at about fifty kilometers an hour, over ground the truck can't handle.
By the army's own count, they fired nine thousand eight hundred and sixty rounds, for nine hundred and eighty-six birds.
That's about ten bullets per emu.
Luckily, the army brought ten thousand bullets. Unluckily, the emus brought twenty thousand emus.
The army went home. The farmers went back to bounties. And the emus never signed a peace treaty.
